question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

As he is not satisfied / with the jury's decision, / he appeal / in the higher court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he appeal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "He" is a third person singular subject, so in the simple present tense the verb must take "-s" → "he appeals".

◦ Correct: As he is not satisfied with the jury's decision, he appeals in the higher court.

• The main clause is in the present tense (matching "is not satisfied"), so the verb should also be present, giving "appeals".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "as he is not satisfied", "with the jury's decision" and "in the higher court" are all correct.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement (simple present): singular subject (he/she/it) + verb-s (he appeals); plural subject (they/we) + base verb (they appeal).

• Remember: only ONE "-s" rule — either the subject is plural OR the verb has "-s", never both.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

He received an honarary degree for his contributions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Honorary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Honorary", meaning given as an honour, without the usual requirements or payment. (मानद / सम्मानार्थ)

◦ Example: The university conferred an honorary doctorate on the scientist.

• Spelling key: HON + OR + ARY — single "n", "-orary" ending.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Honnary", 3 "Honnaary" and 4 "Honnorary" are all misspellings (they wrongly double the "n").

NOTE

• Related words: honour, honourable, honorary, honorarium (a token payment). Note that "honorary" and "honorarium" drop the "u" of "honour".

question: Select the option that has an error in the usage of the present perfect tense.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ravi has complete his homework.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect tense is formed as has/have + past participle (V3). The past participle of "complete" is "completed", not "complete". Hence it must be "Ravi has completed his homework."

◦ Correct: Ravi has completed his homework.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 correctly use "have/has + completed" (the proper past participle).

NOTE

• Present perfect (has/have + V3) connects a past action to the present. Common time markers: already, just, yet, recently, so far, ever, never.

• Do not confuse the base form (complete) with the past participle (completed) after has/have.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mischievious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mischievious" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Mischievous", meaning playfully troublesome or naughty. (शरारती)

◦ Example: The mischievous child hid his sister's shoes.

• Spelling key: MIS + CHIE + VOUS — there is no extra "i" before "-ous" (it is "-vous", not "-vious").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Occurred" (double "r", double "c"), "Questionnaire" (double "n") and "Peculiar" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly mispronounced/misspelt: mischievous (not "mischievious"), grievous (not "grievious"), mischief. Watch out for the wrong extra "i".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Skeleton in the cupboard
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An embarrassing and hidden fact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "skeleton in the cupboard" (or "skeleton in the closet") means a shocking, shameful or embarrassing secret that is kept hidden. (छिपा हुआ शर्मनाक रहस्य)

◦ Example: Every family has a skeleton in the cupboard that they prefer not to discuss.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 miss the key idea of the secret being hidden AND embarrassing/shameful.

NOTE

• Related idioms of secrecy: "let the cat out of the bag" (reveal a secret), "under wraps" (kept secret), "an open secret" (widely known but officially unacknowledged).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

I regret / in notify that / the model you want / is out of stock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in notify that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the verb "regret", when it is followed by another verb of announcing, we use the to-infinitive — "regret to notify/inform/say". Hence "in notify" should be "to notify".

◦ Correct: I regret to notify that the model you want is out of stock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I regret", "the model you want" and "is out of stock" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Regret + to + verb" is used for present/future bad news (I regret to inform you...). "Regret + verb-ing" refers to being sorry about a past action (I regret telling him). The two structures have different meanings.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Through thick and thin
option_1: To pass through thick and thin air
option_2: To be supportive in both good and bad times
option_3: To possess both thick and thin clothes
option_4: To travel through thick and thin clouds
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be supportive in both good and bad times.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "through thick and thin" means through both good and bad times; under all circumstances, remaining loyal and supportive. (हर परिस्थिति में / सुख-दुख में साथ)

◦ Example: A true friend stands by you through thick and thin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 take the idiom literally (air, clothes, clouds) and miss its figurative meaning of steadfast support.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of loyalty/support: "stand by someone", "come rain or shine", "through the ups and downs".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sculpter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sculpter" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Sculptor", meaning an artist who makes sculptures (statues/figures). (मूर्तिकार)

◦ Example: The sculptor carved a beautiful statue out of marble.

• Spelling key: SCULP + TOR — the ending is "-or", not "-er".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Pursuit", "Almighty" and "Stampede" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: sculpt (verb), sculpture (the artwork), sculptor (the artist). Many "doer" nouns end in "-or": actor, doctor, editor, sculptor, inventor, director.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

When Shina reached the bus stand, she realised that she has left her wallet at home.
option_4: she had been left her wallet
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. she had left her wallet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two past actions occur, the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3) and the later action takes the simple past. Leaving the wallet happened before she reached the bus stand, so it needs the past perfect — "she had left her wallet".

◦ Correct: When Shina reached the bus stand, she realised that she had left her wallet at home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because "has left" (present perfect) clashes with the past-tense context.

• Option 3 "leaves" (present) is wrong tense.

• Option 4 "had been left" is a wrong passive construction.

NOTE

• Rule: In a sentence with two past events, use past perfect (had + V3) for the one that happened first, and simple past for the one that happened later.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: He is famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
option_2: He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
option_3: He is more famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
option_4: He is more famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "contribution" collocates with the preposition "to" (a contribution to something), not "for". Hence "contributions to weekly magazines".

• The adjective "famous" here needs no comparative ("more famous") because no comparison with another person is being made.

◦ Correct: He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 use the wrong preposition "for" after "contributions".

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly add "more" (comparative) with no "than" comparison.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "famous for" (a quality/work), "contribution to" (a cause/field), "contribute to" something.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The corporator gathered heaps of curses, and his misdeeds can never be forgiven by the people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Transgressions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Misdeeds" means wrongful or wicked acts; offences. Its closest synonym is "transgressions" — violations of law, duty or moral principle. (कुकर्म / अपराध)

◦ Example: The leader's misdeeds/transgressions cost him public trust.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Consequences" (results), Option 2 "Arguments" (disputes) and Option 4 "Confrontation" (a hostile encounter) do not mean wrongful acts.

NOTE

• Synonyms of misdeed: transgression, wrongdoing, offence, crime, sin, misconduct.

• "Transgress" (verb) = to go beyond a limit / to break a law or moral code.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

It is a betterment of his work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Worsening.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Betterment" means an improvement or the act of making something better. Its antonym is "worsening", meaning becoming worse or deteriorating. (सुधार का विलोम — बिगड़ना)

◦ Example: The reforms aimed at the betterment of the poor, but poor planning led to a worsening of their condition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Growth" and Option 3 "Improvement" are synonyms of betterment.

• Option 1 "Popularity" is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of betterment: improvement, enhancement, upliftment, amelioration.

• Antonyms: worsening, deterioration, decline, degradation.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Sarah said that she hates it when people ______ at her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. stare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stare" means to look fixedly at someone or something for a long time. It fits the context and takes the preposition "at" — "when people stare at her". (घूरना)

◦ Example: It is rude to stare at strangers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "star" (a celestial body / to feature) and Option 4 "stair" (a step) are unrelated homophones.

• Option 3 "steer" (to guide/drive) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Beware of homophones: stare (to gaze) / stair (a step); star (in the sky) / steer (to guide). Only "stare at" fits the sense of looking fixedly.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mary appeared for the test. She was waiting anxiously for the test result.
option_2: hitting the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on pins and needles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on pins and needles" means in a state of anxious anticipation or nervous suspense. It exactly replaces "waiting anxiously". (बेचैनी/उत्सुकता से प्रतीक्षा करना)

◦ Example: She was on pins and needles while waiting for the interview call.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a piece of cake" — something very easy.

• Option 2 "hitting the nail on the head" — describing something exactly right.

• Option 4 "jumping through hoops" — doing many difficult things to achieve something.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of anxiety/suspense: "on tenterhooks", "on edge", "with bated breath", "biting one's nails".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

A medicine to counteract the effect of another medicine
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Antidote.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "antidote" is a medicine or remedy taken to counteract the effects of a poison or another substance/medicine. (विषहर / प्रतिविष औषधि)

◦ Example: The doctor administered an antidote to neutralise the snake venom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Alimony" — money paid to a spouse after divorce/separation.

• Option 2 "Antibiotic" — a medicine that kills or stops the growth of bacteria.

• Option 4 "Anticoagulant" — a substance that prevents the clotting of blood.

NOTE

• Useful "anti-" (against) words: antidote (against poison), antibiotic (against bacteria), antiseptic (against germs), antibody, antacid (against acidity).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains grammatical error(s).

At the zoo, a curious child / fed an elephant some peanuts, / while enthusiastic group of the visitors / watched in amazement.
option_1: At the zoo, a curious child
option_2: while enthusiastic group of the visitors
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. while enthusiastic group of the visitors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A singular countable noun ("group") needs an article. The phrase should read "while an enthusiastic group of the visitors".

◦ Correct: ... while an enthusiastic group of the visitors watched in amazement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "At the zoo, a curious child", "fed an elephant some peanuts" and "watched in amazement" are all correct.

NOTE

• Countable singular nouns require a determiner (a/an/the/my/this). Use "an" before a vowel sound — "an enthusiastic group", "an hour", "an honest man".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Contaminate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pollute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contaminate" means to make something impure or dirty by adding a harmful or polluting substance. Its closest synonym is "pollute". (दूषित करना / प्रदूषित करना)

◦ Example: Factory waste can contaminate/pollute river water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Clean" and 2 "purify" are antonyms of contaminate.

• Option 3 "Excel" (to be outstanding) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of contaminate: pollute, taint, infect, defile, adulterate.

• Antonyms: purify, clean, decontaminate, sterilise.

question: From the given options, identify the sentence which is in the positive degree.
option_1: I have a greater idea in this regard.
option_2: His brother is an intelligent boy.
option_3: She is the most beautiful girl of the class.
option_4: They are playing hockey with longer sticks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. His brother is an intelligent boy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The positive degree uses the base (simple) form of an adjective with no comparison — here "intelligent" is used plainly to describe the boy.

◦ "His brother is an intelligent boy" — positive degree.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "greater" and Option 4 "longer" are in the comparative degree.

• Option 3 "the most beautiful" is in the superlative degree.

NOTE

• Three degrees of comparison: Positive (tall), Comparative (taller, used with "than"), Superlative (tallest, used with "the"). The positive degree simply describes without comparing.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The ambiguous statement of the leader raised criticism among the public.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Clear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguous" means having more than one possible meaning; unclear or open to interpretation. Its antonym is "clear" — easy to understand and unambiguous. (अस्पष्ट का विलोम — स्पष्ट)

◦ Example: The instructions were so ambiguous that no one knew what to do; a clear set of steps would have helped.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Confusing" and Option 4 "Puzzled" are close in sense to ambiguous, not opposite.

• Option 2 "Disorganised" (lacking order) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambiguous: vague, unclear, equivocal, obscure.

• Antonyms: clear, explicit, unambiguous, definite, lucid.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

From contacting our loved ones to buying groceries for our daily needs, mobile phones fulfilled our every requirement during the COVID-19 pandemic. Not only during the pandemic, but mobile phones have also _______ our needs since the time of their invention.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. served.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Served" means fulfilled a need or was useful for a purpose. It fits the positive context of mobile phones meeting our needs. (सेवा की / उपयोगी रहा)

◦ Example: This old car has served us well for ten years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "exasperated" (greatly irritated), Option 3 "annoyed" (irritated) and Option 4 "incensed" (made very angry) all carry a negative sense that contradicts the positive tone of the passage.

NOTE

• "Serve" collocations: serve a purpose, serve one's needs, serve the nation, serve customers. Here it means to be useful and meet requirements.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the auxiliary "had", so it needs the past participle (V3) to form the past perfect tense — "had gone". (go – went – gone)

◦ Correct: My parents and younger sister had gone to my uncle's house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "went" is the simple past (V2) and cannot follow "had".

• Option 3 "go" (base form) and Option 4 "going" (-ing form) do not fit after "had".

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3). The verb "go" forms: go (V1) – went (V2) – gone (V3).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. spend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the to-infinitive marker "to" (expressing purpose) — "to my uncle's house to spend the day". After "to", we use the base form of the verb. (दिन बिताने के लिए)

◦ Correct: ... had gone to my uncle's house to spend the day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spent" (past), Option 3 "spends" (present -s) and Option 4 "spending" (-ing) cannot follow the infinitive "to".

NOTE

• The infinitive of purpose (to + base verb) explains why something is done: "She went to the market to buy vegetables".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage narrates a past event ("At 5:00 p.m, someone ___ the door bell"), so the simple past tense is needed. The simple past of "ring" is "rang". (ring – rang – rung)

◦ Correct: At 5:00 p.m, someone rang the door bell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ring" (base) and Option 2 "rings" (present -s) are present tense.

• Option 4 "rung" is the past participle (V3), which needs "has/have/had" before it.

NOTE

• Verb forms: ring (V1) – rang (V2) – rung (V3). Use V2 (rang) for a simple past action; use V3 (rung) only with has/have/had.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Mr. Sinha" is third person singular, and the sentence is in the past continuous tense ("was + standing"). Hence the correct auxiliary is "was". (एकवचन कर्ता → was)

◦ Correct: Mr. Sinha was standing with his suitcase.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "were" is used with plural subjects (they/we/you), not the singular "Mr. Sinha".

• Option 4 "is" (present) breaks the past-tense narration; Option 3 "been" needs "has/have/had" before it.

NOTE

• Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing. Use "was" with I/he/she/it (singular) and "were" with you/we/they (plural).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Between" is used when referring to two things or people. Since the choice is among two items (coffee and tea), "between" is correct — "his preference between coffee and tea". (दो के बीच)

◦ Correct: I asked his preference between coffee and tea.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "among" is used for more than two things.

• Options 3 "on" and 4 "around" do not fit the sense of choosing between two options.

NOTE

• Rule: between → two persons/things (between you and me); among → more than two (among the students). This between/among distinction is a favourite SSC topic.
